argument_summary: The admissible record does not support clean certification, but it does support narrowing the claim to caveated certification on a risk-managed basis. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.3 percentage points, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and there is a defined mitigation concept with monitoring and rollback if the clinical coding assistant issue worsens. The unresolved weakness is concentrated in observation-status coding guidance, so the central issue is disclosure sufficiency and mitigation completeness, not aggregate launch readiness. The audit concern should therefore be framed as a caveat and disclosure-governance gap rather than a complete failure of launch support.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim is made that business cost changes the policy standard. The practical value of avoiding escalation here is limited to handling a bounded disclosure and mitigation-completeness issue through caveat and follow-up rather than treating the entire release as unsupported.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy text distinguishes clean certification from certification with caveats. Clean certification requires either no material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The current draft runbook does not satisfy that clean-certification predicate because owner and threshold remain TBD. At the same time, the admissible evidence supports the narrower position that certification can proceed only if treated as caveated, with the limitation disclosed for the named launch use case unless and until it is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
concessions: The current record does not support clean certification under the stated policy standard.
The draft mitigation runbook is incomplete because the accountable owner and alert threshold are still TBD.
The model-card draft is currently misaligned with the evidence because it says there are no known material limitations while reviewer comments flag the clinical coding assistant issue.
Public governance guidance on monitoring and model-card content is supportive context, not a substitute for the internal certification requirement.
